memory_update.text: Energy Layer 1 universe should remain multi-lane: grid hardware and structures, transformer/power-quality equipment, high-voltage/HVDC components, nuclear fuel-cycle constraints, and second-order supplier-risk nodes.

Transmission line fittings and conductor-support hardware remain the highest-ranked underfollowed grid chokepoint because PLPC maps directly to physical products installed before line crews arrive and has few obvious public substitutes.

Dry-type transformers, power-quality products, and electrical magnetics are promising underfollowed nodes for AI/data-center power demand, but HPS.A requires primary-source verification before confidence can rise.
HVDC reactors and high-voltage power-quality equipment deserve a global small/mid-cap screen; QPEEL is a promising but still weakly verified candidate.
Utility structures are an investable adjacent layer to line fittings; ACA and VMI provide public-market mappings that may capture physical grid-buildout bottlenecks.

Nuclear fuel-cycle exposure must be separated into conversion, enrichment/HALEU, and advanced fuel fabrication; HON is an embedded conversion reference, while BWXT is a better direct advanced-nuclear reference but not underfollowed.

Before Layer 2, validate market caps, liquidity, revenue purity, backlog, lead times, customer concentration, and qualification barriers for each candidate; do not let reference leaders crowd out underfollowed physical-infrastructure suppliers.

summary: Merged Layer 1 Energy universe from node-level candidates across grid hardware, transmission structures, power-quality equipment, data-center/industrial electrification equipment, nuclear fuel-cycle constraints, advanced nuclear fabrication, and second-order supplier-risk lanes. The ranked universe intentionally balances reference leaders that validate demand and pricing with underfollowed small/mid-cap or niche suppliers closer to physical chokepoints. Highest Serenity relevance currently sits in transmission line hardware, dry-type transformers and power-quality products, utility structures, HVDC/high-voltage equipment, and nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks. Evidence quality remains uneven: PLPC, ACA, HUBB, MYRG, and several reference names have stronger public-source support in the provided Layer 1B material, while HPS.A and QPEEL remain promising but require primary-source verification.
